sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 0-based index in reading order (location order below; row-major within a table, walking each row top-to-bottom in its printed order and left-to-right across that row's own-result columns), giving a population of 0..244 (245 cells). A row named for a competitor architecture contributes only the speed/memory column the paper's own text says the authors measured themselves ('measured' cells below); its accuracy/AP/mIoU stays a baseline and is not in the population. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(245), 15) drew {0, 1, 12, 13, 24, 28, 82, 90, 98, 106, 107, 121, 147, 152, 240} = 1-based {1, 2, 13, 14, 25, 29, 83, 91, 99, 107, 108, 122, 148, 153, 241}.

frame_locations.label: Figure 2 (roadmap bar chart)
frame_locations.notes: Foreground bars = ResNet-50/Swin-T regime, gray bars = ResNet-200/Swin-B regime; both series print per-bar accuracy labels, but they are the exact same 18-step roadmap tabulated precisely (with FLOPs and, for the R50 regime, mean±std over 3 seeds) in Table 10 and Table 11. Text extraction cannot reliably re-attach a floating bar label to its bar and step, and the page-image budget was spent on tables the text could not resolve at all rather than re-deriving numbers a table already gives exactly; counted as 0 here to avoid inventing precision Table 10/11 already state, not because the chart lacks values.

The other 6 are the throughput column on the 6 Swin rows; the surrounding prose is explicit and first-person -- 'We now benchmark them on the more advanced A100 GPUs' -- so this table's baseline-row throughput is the least ambiguous of the four. Every accuracy value in this table duplicates a cell already counted in Table 1; both are counted, following this file's general rule of counting each printed instance of a number as its own frame member.

labels.notes: "achieving 87.8% ImageNet top-1 accuracy and outperforming Swin Transformers on COCO detection and ADE20K segmentation...". The abstract does not itself name the model variant; the value matches Table 1 (lower)'s ConvNeXt-XL row at 384² (ImageNet-22K pretrained, ImageNet-1K finetuned) exactly.

"...increased the performance of the ResNet-50 model from 76.1% [1] to 78.8% (+2.7%), implying that a significant portion of the performance difference...". 76.1% is the standard PyTorch ResNet-50 checkpoint accuracy, cited to [1] (a baseline, not labelled). 78.8% is the authors' own retraining with an enhanced (ViT-style) recipe, restated with more precision in Table 10's 'ResNet-50 (enhanced recipe)' row as 78.82 ± 0.07.

"Here we remove two BatchNorm (BN) layers, leaving only one BN layer before the conv 1x1 layers. This further boosts the performance to 81.4%, already surpassing Swin-T's result." Restates Table 10's 'fewer norms' row (81.41 ± 0.09), rounded to one decimal.
